title: the gate rows whose face has no writer: a face-level defect measured as a ladder of naming rules, so 'unreproducible' can never be quoted from one rung
verdict_reason: the published lookup reports 24 of 196 rows (12.24 pct) and 3 of 51 faces writer-less. A rule that demands a writer rather than a mention reports 163 rows / 23 faces, format templates take that to 10 rows / 7 faces, and composed paths to 0 / 0. So the published lookup OVER-credits (its stem fallback accepts a bare mention: 139 rows are orphan under writer evidence but named under it) while the strictest rule is the one that orphans the most faces -- the ladder is monotone only from the second rung, and 'no writer' is a fact about a named rule, never about the repository.
